gloss: An illustration of how saliva-making nerve fibres, after injury, can grow into the sweat glands of the skin over the gland. Drawn as lines because it is a mechanism, not a measured structure.
role: After injury, the nerve fibres that should make saliva can grow into the sweat glands of the skin, so that eating makes the skin over the gland sweat.
matters: Sweating and flushing over the cheek when eating is common after parotid surgery if you test for it, but fewer people notice it themselves.
